claude.request:
Today's international headlines:
- US death row inmate Christa Pike awake and speaking after failed execution, lawyers say: Experts and lawyers called the apparent recovery unprecedented, noting she is believed to be the only known person to survive a lethal injection.
- Residents of kibbutz destroyed in 7 October Hamas-led attacks grapple with how to rebuild: Three years on from the attack on Nir Oz, in which 47 people were killed and 76 taken hostage, some survivors have returned to live there.
- What is pneumonic plague and how does it spread?: The death of a worker from a Russian lab that researches plague has prompted questions about the disease.
- Ex-US spy who stashed gold bars in his home admits to $200m scam: David Rush, who also confessed to providing secrets to a foreign government, had revealed the existence of a "clandestine human source", prosecutors said.
- A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows: A sharp increase in human activity is affecting the way the Himalayan monal lives and communicates, studies show.
- Former Australian bishop jailed for sexually abusing young men: The former Bishop of Broome is one of the most senior Catholic clerics in the world to face sex abuse charges.
- Tear gas in Paris and Marseille as school protests grow across France: Crowds of mainly teenagers called for more resources for schools and an end to what they called police repression.
- Pornhub returns to Australia but only for adults with Apple devices: The world's most popular porn site went dark in March in Australia due to age verification laws.
- Former German spy chief arrested for espionage and treason: August Hanning is accused of obtaining classified information for a foreign power.
- 'Ghost particles' from space telescope wins physics Nobel: Belgian physicist Prof Francis Halzen has won for his pioneering work on an observatory that detects particles from space.
- White House defends Trump comment to let Iran 'take out' LA and San Diego: Gavin Newsom called the remarks "deranged", but the White House said Trump was warning of the risk of a nuclear Iran.
- Many Nepalis swept away in the floods aren't officially dead, leaving families in limbo: Relatives are finding themselves with no compensation and facing an administrative nightmare.
